spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates what a linear backing store actually changes — compositing (globalCompositeOperation 'lighter') and resampling (drawImage decimation), the operations named in the feature's own motivation — and explicitly measures that gradients do NOT change (they interpolate in sRGB per spec, midpoint stored as linear 54), preventing the obvious misreading.

interactive.rationale: Two intensity sliders re-render three panels live with sampled-pixel readouts; a downscale button runs the checkerboard experiment; every number shown is measured via getImageData, not asserted.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Card promises lighter-compositing plus checkerboard decimation with a JavaScript math half that works everywhere and a native half that only claims to run where it does — the page does exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers clamp blowout past 100% summed light, the unsupported branch (dashed panel with the real TypeError text and exact enable steps), the deceptive-similarity zone at low intensities called out in copy, and the gradient non-difference.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5122501071994880, the spec colour-spaces section, and CSS Color 4's srgb-linear definition.

conformance.rationale: Covered by the feature-level suite (accept-and-echo, baseline, conversion, negative enum contract); this page's native panels gate on the same accept-and-echo check the suite encodes.

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this environment; verified per the routine toolset with headless Chromium 141 via Bash + CDP. Unflagged: sRGB overlap 255 vs linear-math 176 at 50%+50% (physics 176), checkerboard 127 vs computed 188, unsupported panel showing the real TypeError. Flagged (--enable-experimental-web-platform-features unlocks srgb-linear on 141): native panel activates, lighter agreement message fires, and the native checkerboard measured 187 vs the true 188 — the native half was exercised for real, not simulated. Desktop + emulated 360×740 DPR3 screenshots; zero page exceptions.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts on every slider render (lights-rendered, comparing math sample to the physics expectation) and on the downscale run, plus a failure branch if init throws.

design_system.rationale: UI colours all from CSS variables (canvas contents are the demo subject); buttons keep bg+color; tags use emerald/blue/amber text on paper at bold small-caps sizes meeting AA; canvas[hidden] display:none guards the panel toggle against the page-local canvas display rule.

accessibility.rationale: Every canvas has role=img with aria-labelledby to its visible heading and aria-describedby to the shared aria-live reading that carries the sampled numbers, so the visual state has a full numeric text equivalent; sliders are native, labelled, with visible value readouts; the transfer-function pre is tabbable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360×740 DPR3: documentElement scrollWidth 360 (the one wide element is a code line inside the pre's own overflow-x scroller, which is the sanctioned pattern); panels stack single-column; canvases scale to column width while getImageData sampling stays in backing pixels; desktop 1280 shows three panels side by side.

openQuestions.title: Exercise display-p3-linear native compositing on a Chrome 155 binary
openQuestions.detail: The native panels gate on srgb-linear only, which is the space whose success path was verifiable on this Chromium 141 behind the experimental flag. display-p3-linear does not exist in the 141 binary at all, so its native compositing behaviour (identical mechanism, wider primaries) is asserted by the conformance suite but not yet demonstrated in a panel. On a 155 binary, consider a toggle between the two linear spaces in this page's panels.

openQuestions.title: Show alpha compositing (source-over with translucency) in linear space
openQuestions.detail: The page demonstrates additive 'lighter' and resampling. Ordinary source-over blending of translucent colors also happens in the backing space and is the case most UI developers hit (dark halos around anti-aliased edges). A small additive stage blending a translucent white over black in both spaces would round out the operation coverage.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible canvas demo with text alternatives and live region readouts
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Canvas-only state must have a text equivalent; associate it via aria-describedby and announce changes through a polite live region rather than re-labelling the canvas.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All six canvases carry role=img + aria-labelledby/aria-describedby; sampled pixel values and the physics expectation are written to aria-live=polite outputs on every interaction.

guidanceConsulted.query: wide gamut and HDR canvas color management
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Constrain intrinsic-width content: grid items need min-width:0 and long tokens need overflow-wrap so a single string cannot widen the page.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied after a first verification round caught the flag string widening the third panel: .panel{min-width:0}, overflow-wrap:anywhere on the flagnote/unsupported/reading text; re-verified scrollWidth 360 at mobile width.

summary: The practical concept: the same two operations measured on gamma and linear backing stores, with the linear math shown and run in JavaScript so every browser sees the difference, and the native half activating only where getContext really echoes srgb-linear — verified in both states on Chromium 141, including the flagged success path where native results matched the math (176/176 lighter, 187 vs 188 decimation).
